#4049. GTA 6 Takes Over PS5's Welcome Page, Including a New Set of Wallpapers

Sony and Rockstar Games are making damn sure you know GTA 6 has just launched, as the PS5's Welcome hub — the landing page for the console — has been taken over by the new game.

The page's icon currently has that telltale pink/orange gradient and palm trees, and before you see your usual assortment of widgets, a new panel promoting GTA 6 appears.

You can dismiss it if you don't want to see it, and there's also an option to view the game, which takes you to its PS Store page.

Scroll down and you'll find your usual Welcome dashboard, but there's also a new icon here, letting you know there are new, GTA 6-related backgrounds available.

Click through and you'll see a GTA 6 folder, which contains five new wallpapers with which you can decorate your Welcome hub. They're all in that signature illustrated style, with most featuring protagonists Jason and Lucia.

It's always nice to get more backgrounds for the Welcome page, and this game getting special treatment is no real surprise.

#4048. The Petit Planet beta is coming back with new updates, but you still need to hope for an invite

If you've been missing Petit Planet since it was last available to play, you'll be happy to know that HoYoverse is hosting another test soon.

It’s been quite a while since we’ve heard anything about Petit Planet, the upcoming game from Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail developer HoYoverse. By most accounts, Petit Planet is the studio’s take on Animal Crossing, though with a few interesting ideas of its own.

The game’s most recent test took place all the way back in November, but its next big test isn’t far off.

HoYoverse announced today that Petit Planet’s Stardrift Test is scheduled for April 21. This latest build will be available on PC, Android, and iOS. The beta will include new Neighbors, an updated Starsea Voyage, and more for you to do at the Galactic Bazaar.

Seeing as interacting with Neighbors is a core part of this life sim RPG, the confirmation that new faces will be available in this test is big news. Each Neighbor in Petit Planet is a character, with their own personalty and life story.

The Starsea Voyage now includes a map, too, which you can use to take you to other Islets. If you played any of the previous tests, you should already be familiar with this feature.

The only bit of bad news here is that this remains a closed beta. You’re still encouraged to sign up on the official website, but you’re not guaranteed access. HoYoverse said that only a portion of players who sign up will be invited to the upcoming beta.

Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.

Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, has published GTA 6's day-one retail sales, and they're predictably astronomical and record-breaking.

Via BusinessWire, Rockstar and Take-Two announce that GTA 6's launch day sales, based on estimates through end of day on November 19, reached $3.79 billion, surpassing any other launch across all entertainment mediums and officially making GTA 6 the biggest entertainment launch of all time.

The companies also reveal that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies pre-release, which is another "new record across all platforms." For comparison, 2022 Game of the Year Elden Ring sold 30 million copies in three years.

"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," says Rockstar co-founder and GTA veteran Sam Houser. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you."

Even though the industry has been anticipating GTA 6 to be the biggest game of all time, and very possibly the biggest entertainment product ever, for a while now based on the game's estimated budget of $1-1.5 billion, seeing these numbers become official is staggering.

Elden Ring was a massively successful game when it released back in 2022, and seeing its near-lifetime sales be eclipsed by GTA 6 in a single day is truly astounding no matter how inevitable Rockstar's success has always seemed.

#4046. Heartopia celebrates 30 million downloads with new outfits, permanent price cuts

Heartopia's rise has continued since its launch earlier this year, and the game's developer isn't slowing down with updates.

Heartopia has kicked off a new event to celebrate passing 30 million downloads. Just a couple of weeks after delivering the vintage Hollywood-themed Dreamlight Cinematics event, developer XD Games has revealed The Whimsical Tea Party, a limited-time Gilded Acorn Exhibition.

The event kicked off on Saturday, bringing some new themed content to the game.

Whimsical Tea Party’s biggest addition are the new outfits, including the Wandering Traveler, and the Duke Bunny outfits. Each outfit is available in three different colours. Another thing Heartopia events bring are building materials sets.

This one adds the Labyrinth furniture building materials set, the Hedgehog & Flamingo mallet, and the Cheshire Cat pet costume. Speaking of outfits, XD Games is dropping the in-game prices for a number of items permanently.

All original pet outfits now cost 66.7% less. Those of the Common variety will now cost 10 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, instead of the previous 30. Rare pet outfits will cost 5 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, down from 15.

If you happened to buy Common or Rare original pet outfits between July 17, 2024 and March 22, 2026, you’ll be refunded the difference. This will automatically show up in-game the next time you log in. If you instead purchased those pet outfits between March 23 and April 4, you should look forward to your refund before April 10.

Keeping with the theme of freebies, Heartopia is also celebrating surpassing 30 million downloads worldwide by giving all players a small gift package in-game. This freebie is available until May 29, so you should have enough time to claim it.

#4045. Honkai: Star Rail players are eating good, with Version 4.2 and third anniversary celebrations kicking off later this month

Honkai: Star Rail will be celebrating its third anniversary just days after it delivers a major update, and there's quite a bit to chew on in this one.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The big inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

As for the big third anniversary celebration, it will kick off in-game on April 26, bringing back Festive Gifts. The event will only be available during these celebrations, and it will once again be gifting players who log in regularly a total of 20 pulls.

You’ll also be able to a select a blessing card from a companion of your choice to receive a special gift of 1,600 Stellar Jades. The same celebrations will also seeHuohuo and Robin permanently added to the Stellar Convergence store. You’ll have another chance to exchange a Golden Companion Spirit for any companion you like in that store, too — and all you need to do is log in anytime between Versions 4.2 and 4.4. This being a new year for Honkai: Star Rail, the top-up double bonus is resetting, meaning anyone who tops up their wallet will get a hefty bonus.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 launches and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

#4044. Pokémon-Like Temtem's Bullet Heaven Spin-Off Arrives On Switch Next Year

Crema Games' Temtem was one of the better Pokémon-likes we had played when it arrived on Switch back in 2022. The dev released its final update a couple of years back, but soon, we'll get a chance to play its Survivors-style spinoff.

Temtem: Swarm launches on Switch on 21st January 2027 after coming to Steam back in April. An initial glance made us think this was Crema's take on Pokémon Unite, but on closer inspection, it's far more Vampire Survivors.

This one sees you choose your Pokémon Tem fighter and face off against swarms of corrupted creatures to survive for as long as you can. There are mini-bosses to tackle along the way, and a stream of upgrades and abilities to keep you on your toes as you progress through runs.

Excitingly, the Switch version will launch with full cross-platform co-op, so you'll be able to team up with pals on PC or PS5 right from the jump.

Here's a brief rundown of the game's key features and a handful of screenshots:

Team Up to Survive the Swarm: Battle relentless Tem swarms solo or with up to 3 friends in intense co-op! Strategize, share resources, and unleash overpowered synergies to defeat bosses. Booming Boss Battles: Conquer unique stages by strategizing against challenging mini-bosses and epic stage bosses. Face iconic Temtem like Gharunder, Yowlar, and Nessla in hand-crafted stages. Unleash Unstoppable Ultimates: Unleash devastating attacks, defensive abilities, or map-clearing power-ups with each Tems Ultimate ability. Master timing and unleash these incredible powers to turn the tide of battle. Evolve to Endure: Earn XP, level up your Temtem, and unlock powerful final evolutions. Each evolution grants massive boosts to skills and strength for ultimate survival. Discover All the Tems: Collect and capture every Temtem to unlock powerful Traits and unique Ultimates. Master each Temtem in solo and co-op to overcome any challenge. Revive and Thrive: No fear of defeat! Support fallen teammates in Ghost Mode until they can revive you to rejoin the fight. Online co-op ensures the adventure never ends, even after a tough encounter.

We had a good enough time with Temtem on Switch back in 2022, and the Survivors-like spin-off is an interesting idea on the surface. A 'Mostly Positive' review streak on Steam has us hopeful that it'll be worth a look in the early days of 2027.

#4043. 'Gears & GTA 6 May Have Provided A Temporary Reprieve' - Xbox Hardware Sales Get A Major Surge In The US

"Higher pricing was the primary driver of the dollar sales growth"

Xbox hardware sales were up 42% in October in the U.S. year-over-year. It's been donkeys since we've seen positive news attached to this level of stonks coming out of Microsoft, so we'll take it!

The figures were shared in a monthly report from the statistical boffins over at Circana. Mat Piscatella revealed that US hardware spending was up by 2% compared to October last year. PlayStation 5 sales grew by 20%, Switch 2 dropped 11%, and Xbox Series surged by 42%. Phwoar!

Hardware - Hardware spending increased by 2% versus a year ago, to $357M. October growth in PlayStation 5 (+20%) and Xbox Series (+42%) dollar sales when compared to a year ago offset a drop in Switch 2 (-11%).

However, Piscatella made sure to point out that "higher pricing was the primary driver of dollar sales growth" for Xbox Series, as "XBS unit sales grew by 10%" whilst the average selling price also bumped up by 29%.

Hardware - Higher pricing was the primary driver of the dollar sales growth on both PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series. PS5 unit sales increased by 5% versus a year ago, while its average selling price (ASP) increased by 13%. XBS unit sales grew by 10% vs YA, while its ASP jumped 29%.

Xbox's planned hardware price increase came into effect back in August, but according to Circana, Gears of War: E-Day and GTA 6 "may have provided at least a temporary reprieve" for the console's sales figures.

"It’s no secret that Xbox Series hardware sales have struggled in recent years. Gears and GTA may have provided at least a temporary reprieve."

Gears of War: E-Day appears to be something of a console mover, and I'd wager help from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 played a part too. Microsoft has claimed the top two spots in Circana's projected best-selling video games chart for October 2026, taking both physical and digital dollar sales into consideration.

October 2026 U.S. Projected Top 10 Best-Selling Games Ranked on Physical & Full Game Digital Dollar Sales (Excludes Mobile and Digital Add-On Content)

Modern Warfare 4 was the best-selling game of October, which Piscatella also noted makes it the "19th consecutive year that a Call of Duty franchise release has been the best-selling game of its debut month".

#4042. GTA 6 Has an Easy Mode Buried in an Impressive Range of Accessibility Options

GTA 6 is easily the most customisable game that Rockstar has ever made when it comes to accessibility options.

There's a wide range of settings and toggles to experiment with, in a bid to make the open world experience more comfortable. And while the initiative isn't quite as in-depth as what you'll find in recent Ubisoft or Sony-published titles, it's still a solid step forward for the studio.

But there are a couple of settings in particular that have raised eyebrows. As you might know, Rockstar never deals in difficulty levels; outside of things like adjustable aim assist, you're always in line with the developer's intended challenge.

In GTA 6, however, there are two difficulty-related toggles buried in the accessibility options: 'Accessible Combat' and 'Reduced Vehicle Damage'.

In essence, both settings amount to having an easy mode. Accessible Combat decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider.

Meanwhile, Reduced Vehicle Damage does exactly what it says on the tin, making your chosen ride more durable.

But just how much easier do these toggles make GTA 6? The options menu itself issues a warning, stating that when enabled, the "balance and experience" of the game is "significantly" changed.

We've put them to the test, and despite some claims I've seen floating around the internet this morning, they do not make you invincible. You still need to play the game as intended — actually taking cover in firefights, for example — but the overall level of challenge is still noticeably reduced.

The idea is that these toggles will allow less experienced, mentally fatigued, or disabled players to progress without too much friction.

And just to be clear, enabling these settings does not disable Trophies. The bottom line here is that if you're having trouble getting through GTA 6, these options should almost certainly help.

Speaking of help, you can check out our overall GTA 6 guide and our totally spoiler-free Tips & Tricks guide for assistance with everything from collectibles to neat gameplay features you may not know about.

As for the other accessibility settings on offer, Rockstar's covered a lot of ground. For starters, there are a bunch of aim assist and lock on options, while button taps and presses can be customised to an impressive extent, to make them less physically demanding.

You can even toggle "simplified" minigames, making the controls less complex, and there are multiple ways to customise controller layouts.

On top of that, a multitude of low vision options are available, there's a one-toggle brightness modifier, and there's a dedicated high contrast setting. Again, it's good stuff from the developer.

Have you been adjusting any of these options for your playthrough of GTA 6? Are you happy to see Rockstar adopting a more accessible approach? Snap to your target in the comments section below.

Shanghai police have reportedly made 140 arrests this year alone related to counterfeit toys

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Police in Shanghai, China have reportedly arrested 13 people in connection with an alleged criminal scheme selling counterfeit Final Fantasy 7 figures.

First reported by local Shanghai-based publication Shangguan News (translation via Automaton), in May Shanghai police began receiving complaints about Final Fantasy 7 Tifa Lockhart figures purchased from an online store that didn't match-up with the official toys licensed by rights holder Square Enix. Police reportedly verified with Square Enix that the seller had not been authorized to sell the figures, which appear to be nearly identical to an official Square Enix product, although seemingly without the articulation points that allow you to change the position of arms and legs. Here's a comparison via Dexerto's Twitter account:

Police have arrested 13 people accused of selling counterfeit Final Fantasy 7 Tifa Lockhart figures The Chinese sellers reportedly charged higher prices by including extra faces, hands, and accessories not found with the official figures https://t.co/AE1IyS0wi9November 19, 2026

According to Shangguan News, officially licensed figures typically don't include customization accessories because of the added copyright and production costs, but since counterfeiters don't have to worry about that stuff, they're able to add things like swappable face plates and other accessories and then sell the toys for more than their genuine counterparts. Police say the Tifa Lockhart operation in particular had been worth more than 2 million yuan, which is roughly $300,00, at the time of the arrests. The 13 suspects involved are said to be under investigation for alleged trademark infringement.

Shanghai police have reportedly busted more than 30 similar cases of counterfeit figures or figurines in 2026 alone, resulting in more than 140 arrests and 70 million yuan, or $10.5 million, in seized assets.

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation boss says the story isn't being "shaped by fan reactions," but the devs are using feedback on "the overall gameplay experience"

#4040. Animal Crossing: New Horizons gets a new item to celebrate 25 years of the series

The allegedly finished game might finally, truly be feature complete with the addition of an anniversary item.

Animal Crossing: New Horizons has received a surprise patch today to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the life sim series. The update, version 3.0.2, is available across the Switch and Switch 2 versions of the game.

The patch brings a single new addition to New Horizons - a leaf item. Everyone gets it, too, so you don’t have to do anything special to acquire it.

After installing the patch, simply head to your in-house mailbox to claim it. The mail includes a hearty message to fans who supported the series for years, featuring an appropriate Nintendo N64 stamp.

The Leaf Statue, as it’s referred to in-game, lights up when placed.

April 14, 2011 marks the release of the original, lesser-known version of Animal Crossing in Japan. The game was initially released as Animal Forest (Dobutsu no Mori) on the Nintendo N64, before later making its way to the Nintendo GameCube in December of the same year as Dobutsu no Mori+ with some extra features.

That same, original design of the package is also available for display in your game. The rest of the patch notes are entirely about various bug fixes, so not much more there. You can see the full change log on Nintendo’s support website.

#4039. Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

Metro 2039 takes us back to the tunnels of the Moscow Metro where, fittingly, Nazi ideology never died.

The Metro series is finally, officially back with a new installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

#4038. Blizzard will talk about Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred one last time before the expansion's launch next week

We're well under two weeks from the launch of Diablo 4's next expansion, Lord of Hatred, but there's more yet to be said.

Diablo 4 is mere days away from the launch of its biggest expansion yet, and Blizzard wants to make sure it got one last chance to tell you about it. Lord of Hatred is the follow-up to 2024’s Vessel of Hatred, and it’s set to arrive on April 28.

Next week, however, we’re getting an updated look at the new content as part of a livestream. This is the Developer Update kind; the meaty, information-dense show anyone who follows Diablo’s livestreams should be familiar with.

The next Developer Update is set for Thursday, April 23. It’ll kick off at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 6pm GMT. The show will, naturally, focus on Lord of Hatred. In particular, we’re getting another look at the expansion content that hasn’t been given the same level of coverage as the bigger features.

Everyone knows about the new Skovos region, the Warlock class (and the Paladin before that), but we haven’t seen much from the other gameplay-altering features that affect a lot of the core flow.

In next week’s showcase, Blizzard will show off the updated and expanded skill trees - which come to all classes, the Talisman system, and the gear-altering Horadric Cube. War Plans, the new make-your-own-endgame feature will be discussed, too.

More interestingly, we’re also going to hear about the new season kicking off right alongside the launch of Lord of Hatred. A short, in-betweener season is currently live in Diablo 4, and it’s going to end right as the next one/the expansion launch.

And, of course, the show won’t end before the team takes a few questions from chat, as is tradition. If you want to catch it live, you’ll be able to do so on Diablo’s official YouTube, Twitch, Twitter, and TikTok channels.

#4037. Call of Duty's Influence Is Fading Fast as Modern Warfare 4 Fails to Make US Top 10

There's been an awful lot of debate about the overall quality and lasting commercial success of Call of Duty across the last few years, with many arguing that the once unstoppable series is steadily losing its edge.

As such, this latest report from Circana won't make for easy reading if you're Xbox or Activision.

According to the ever-informative Mat Piscatella, the recently released Modern Warfare 4 was the best selling game of October in the US.

However, despite a strong debut and a mostly positive reception — especially with regards to its single player campaign — the big budget shooter has failed to break into the top 10 best selling titles of 2026 so far.

For Call of Duty, such an absence would have been unthinkable just a few short years ago; it really does suggest that it's struggled to match the kind of sales figures we've come to expect of the franchise.

Case in point: the current-gen port of Black Ops 2 remains on 2026's top 10 list.

October 2026 U.S. Video Game Market Highlights Thread from Circana - Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 was the best-selling game of October, marking the 19th consecutive year that a Call of Duty franchise release has been the best-selling game of its debut month.

Of course, there's still time for Modern Warfare 4 to make up some ground with the holidays right around the corner, but this seems to be a continuation of the downward trend that we saw with last year's very poorly rated Black Ops 7.

Indeed, it's possible that the Black Ops 7 backlash has negatively impacted Modern Warfare 4's appeal — and that's not the kind of spiral that Activsion will want to find itself in.

Elsewhere, Gears of War: E-Day — which was famously cancelled on PS5 just weeks ahead of launch — managed second place for October, and the eye-watering Star Wars: Galactic Racer entered in third.

Another new release, the largely fantastic Final Fantasy Resonance, landed in sixth — which feels like a win for Square Enix given the flood of games that came out last month.

* Projected digital sales ^ Actual digital sales

#4036. Zelda Playable & Electric Ocarinas Will Initially Be Sold On An Invite-Only Basis (Europe)

And you'll need to pass the criteria to register interest

We've been keeping an eye out for news of Nintendo's playable and electric ocarinas going on sale in Europe for a good while now. It looks like sales are just around the corner, but you're going to need to jump through some hoops if you want to get your hands on one.

Both the Nintendo playable model and HORI electric version will initially be sold on an invite-only basis in Europe. You can register your interest in getting either model now on the Nintendo website, but there are some criteria that you'll have to pass first.

Firstly, you'll need to have a Nintendo account registered in Europe (excluding Norway, Russia and South Africa), have allowed Nintendo to process your usage information to customise services, offers and recommendations in your Nintendo Account settings, and have allowed Nintendo to send email recommendations about games, events, special offers and more. You'll need to have done all of that by 22nd November.

You can only register your interest if you have "reached at least 10 hours of play time in the Nintendo Switch 2 game The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time by 18/11/2026" using the same Nintendo account you use to register.

And that's just to get an invite. On the day that the products become available, those who are invited will receive an email with a link to purchase either ocarina (limited to one each per customer).

The playable ocarina will set you back £29.99, bundling the instrument with a wrist strap and sheet music for all of the in-game songs. HORI's electric option is a little more expensive at £41.99, but also comes with a dedicated stand.

Reminder Zelda: Ocarina Of Time - Playable Ocarina Available Now On The Nintendo Store

Have you registered your interest for either model? Let us know in the comments.

Jim came to Nintendo Life in 2022 and, despite his insistence that The Minish Cap is the best Zelda game and his unwavering love for the Star Wars prequels (yes, really), he has continued to write news and features on the site ever since.

#4035. Xbox One Players Share Their First Impressions Of GTA 6 Via The Cloud

Here's what it's like using Xbox Cloud Gaming to play on XB1

If you want to play GTA 6 natively on any console right now, you can only do so on Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S or PS5. However, if you're willing to use the cloud, it's possible to play the game on Xbox One.

To do this, you have to buy the game on the Xbox Store first, and then acquire Xbox Cloud Gaming time via one of two means - you either purchase time on the Xbox Store, or you get a subscription to Xbox Game Pass that includes a certain amount of time per-tier (and you can top it up later if you need to).

There is also the option to play "free with ads" using Xbox Cloud Gaming, but we haven't verified that it works with GTA 6 yet (although there's seemingly no reason why it wouldn't), and it only gives you 30 minutes of game time before it kicks you off. Some of GTA 6's missions can last longer than 30 minutes, so that's not really ideal.

Anyway, while we're still in the process of dusting off our Xbox One consoles and trying GTA 6 on there for ourselves, we thought we'd first share some impressions from Xbox fans across the web on what it's been like for them so far.

Let's take a look at what some Xbox One owners are saying about it:

Overall, it seems like most people are enjoying their time with GTA 6 on Xbox One so far, although that's not to say there haven't been issues in some cases. The biggest complaints seem to be that some players think it looks "blurry" (while others don't really see a problem), and there are also a small number of reports that it appears to disconnect for no reason sometimes.

There's also a bit of worry that the servers might not be able to handle the load during "peak" hours, and considering we're only on the first day of GTA 6's official launch, it's hard to say how things are going to go in that regard.

Meanwhile, every other version of Xbox Cloud Gaming officially runs at up to 1080p and 12mbps bitrate.

If you want any further feedback about playing GTA 6 on the Xbox One, we'll aim to get some "hands on" impressions to you ASAP. Based on these initial day one impressions though, it seems to be working fairly well right now.

Keep in mind that you obviously need a strong and consistent internet connection in order to play games via Xbox Cloud Gaming, otherwise you may experience heavy lag, disconnects and all sorts of other problems.

#4034. The Sims 4's much maligned paid mods have made it to consoles, but Kits are coming back to PC

The Sims 4's Marketplace and user-created content have officially arrived on consoles, a little over a month after their debut on PC.

The Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This new feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a new premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

For most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis said that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

Interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

Unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just launched on consoles, the company may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the new paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

#4033. Naval warfare, an actual server browser and more on the way to Battlefield 6 this year as BF Studios reveals 2026 roadmap

2026 is looking very exciting for Battlefield 6, even if much of what's coming is based on things we already know, and some we've long been asking for.

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a plan laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

The video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

We’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is said to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

The introduction of naval combat will bring with it a new dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

#4032. Diablo 4's next season won't have any new mechanics or a new theme because all the focus is on Lord of Hatred

If you don't intend to buy the Lord of Hatred expansion, the next season in Diablo 4 won't be as exciting as you'd expect.

Diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

The game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The new season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each new season.

You’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

The even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The new season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

Blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

In case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

#4031. Ubisoft Confirms 166 Layoffs at Key Assassin's Creed Studios

Ubisoft has confirmed that it's laid off a total of 166 employees across two of its major studios, Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec.

Although this figure only accounts for roughly 4% of the publisher's full Canadian workforce, it's obviously still a lot of people to let go of in one fell swoop.

Based on an unnamed source, IGN reports that the layoffs are largely to do with Ubisoft's continued restructuring; it suggests that many of those impacted were working on projects that have since been cancelled.

For context, Montreal has worked on almost every big Ubisoft game you can think of over the past couple of decades. It's currently developing Assassin's Creed Hexe, having spearheaded Assassin's Creed Valhalla and Assassin's Creed Origins previously.

Quebec, meanwhile, has been chiefly responsible for Assassin's Creed Syndicate, Odyssey, and the series' most recent instalment, Shadows.

"As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs," reads an official statement from Ubisoft.

"Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources," it continues.

This console generation has proven tumultuous for Ubisoft as a whole, to the point where its production pipelines have been completely overhauled under Chinese tech giant Tencent's guidance. The company is still trying to streamline operations more than a year after all of that came into effect.

Naturally, we wish everyone impacted by these layoffs all the best for the future.

#4030. Persona 6 Doesn't Have A Date Yet, But Atlus Says You Won't Have To Wait As Long For Persona 7

There's been a lot of talk around how long GTA fans have been waiting for the latest entry to launch, but Persona isn't actually that far behind. Persona 5 – in its original state – released over a decade ago on 15th September 2016, and although Persona 6 has now been officially announced, we're none the wiser as to when it will actually come out.

It's likely to finally land at some point in 2027 after the dust has settled from Persona 4 Revival, but according to a recent interview with general producer Kazuhisa Wada (thanks, Nintendo Everything), fans won't have to wait quite so long for the inevitable Persona 7.

"We will continue to cherish what makes Persona unique, while also embracing changes in the times and needs, and taking on new challenges. We aim to be a brand that can grow for 5, 10 years, and beyond.

"Among those projects, the one we’re currently working on is Persona 6. While there’s still limited information I can share, we want to prove the results of all the challenges we’ve faced so far through the game itself. With that in mind, we’re creating something even better than before, and we’re feeling a real sense of accomplishment as we work on it.

"And Persona 6 is not the end. We are working on various things to ensure that you don’t have to wait as long for the next installment as we have in the past. And in order to make Persona an even bigger IP, we are constantly thinking about creative ideas and developments that will not disappoint your expectations. Please look forward to what’s to come from Persona.”

We will look forward to it, Wada-san, thank you sir. Let's keep the focus on Persona 4 Revival and Persona 6 for now though, hm?

It's not a surprising statement, mind you. Game development is taking longer than ever these days, which also makes it more expensive than ever. So a lot of publishers are looking into potential solutions to cut down on dev time and increase the cadence of releases. As long as it doesn't involve handing everything off to AI, we're fine with that.

Persona 4 Revival is currently scheduled to launch on Switch 2 on 20th May 2027, a few months after other platforms. As for Persona 6, an imminent reveal has been rumoured recently thanks to a backend update on the official website. Hardly concrete, but it's a start.

#4029. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.8 is refreshing your team comps with a new mechanic, and the game is coming to Steam

Zenless Zone Zero will soon become the first HoYoverse game to make its way to Steam, though we wish we had more details.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next big update, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive company’s debut on Valve’s platform.

The main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as New Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

The release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

The first new Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

The second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver big Physical burst damage.

The higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this update is the new Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

When an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

If you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

The Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a new Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

My understanding, from early reporting, @awp69, is that E-Day had sold over 400k copies, and that was being reported just days after the game released. I'm not sure who is saying 300k, but it's not me. I imagine it has sold still more sine then, and it will sell more still in the current sales.

Now, is 400k a good result on its own for a game that cost at least $300 million to make (with some estimates putting it a lot more than that)? I'd argue no, that would be pretty dismal. However, with that said, we were also led to believe that it had sold 711,000 Premium Upgrades ahead of its launch, which is not to be sniffed at, and obviously we do not know how many more consoles were sold, nor how many more Game Pass subscriptions were sold. Nor do we know how much money people have been spending on the microtransactions either. All of that does add up.

The problem though comes down to simple maths, if E-Day cost $200 million (and bear in mind that is a conservative figure because we are led to believe it cost much more than that to make), but still, if it cost $200 million to make, then the game needs to sell the equivalent of 2,850,000 full priced games in order to just break even, and it is a long way short of that in sheer sales. And of course, if the game cost the reported $300 million then it needs to sell the equivalent of 4,285,000 full priced copies. This is where the problem for the game lies as it is highly unlikely to make back its development costs, which could be very bad news for the studio.

Obviously, we know that a single exclusive is not what it is all about for Xbox; it is about creating an ecosystem that will attract people in considerable numbers, and also ensure that people already here do not want to leave. However, the problem is, there are no exclusive games are on the near horizon that will continue to attract people. It's possible that the Elder Scrolls 6 will be exclusive to Xbox, and a lot of people within these forums are pinning their hopes for Xbox on that game, but the problem there is that ES6 could be several years away.

My honest opinion is that I think that Sharma will look at E-Day's (probably) meagre sales and behind the scenes the decision to reverse course on exclusives will be made, although I do not expect her to tell us this is the case until after Helix releases as I don't think Sharma will want to hurt the sales chances of Helix by publicly admitting that it won't have exclusive games. I say this on the basis that there are no big AAA console selling games on the horizon, and that Helix is likely to release prior to the next big first-party game. I mean, there's not a lot of point in telling us right now that Xbox will no longer have exclusive first-party games when there are none in the near future anyway. She may as well wait until she can no longer avoid telling us that's the case because the game is being put up for pre-orders.

Time will tell, and I'd love to be proven wrong, but I would far rather see studios survive and our favourite games continue to be made, than pursue a self-harming exclusive strategy. Of course, all that could change if (when!) Sharma announces a change in day one first-party Game Pass releases, but I think that should have been done prior to the release of E-Day, and the next big AAA first-party game is probably years away...

To be clear, @awp69, I was not suggesting that sales were as low as 400k. I was just pointing out that where you were mentioning 300k that 400k was being spoken of soon after the release of the game.

I'm not 100% sure how this chart was worked out, and on what it was based; was it based on actual full game sales, or did it also include the 711k+ Premium Upgrades in that figure too?

Truth is, we will never likely know how the game sold because Microsoft keep these things top secret. We don't know what Sharma's expectations for the game were; so we don't know whether she considers 400k sales and 711k Premium Upgrades a strong start. She probably does, but the truth is she is the boss of Xbox, and so she was never going to come out publicly and say sales were a disappointment because she has shareholders to think of, and nothing spooks shareholders more quickly than the Boss saying things are not going well!

As for the game topping the Xbox charts, I guess we have to keep things in perspective here; we know that fewer games are bought on Xbox than elsewhere because of Game Pass, and also the number of Xboxes that are owned as a secondary console or as a Games Pass machine. So it is all relative. E-Day being at or towards the top of the charts could easily be achieved with relatively low numbers.

Honestly, I think we will get a better idea of how the game has performed by how Sharma treats The Coalition in the coming months; if she leaves it untouched or relatively untouched then I think we can assume the game did alright. If she hits the studio hard, then there has to be a reason for that, and the most likely scenario is that the game performed poorly (relative to its budget).

As I have said before, the problem is that the game needs to retain a sizable number of daily players, and judging by Steam alone, which saw just 2,978 players in the past 24 hours, which is a drop of more than 90% in little over a month, then E-Day is not retaining its players. Plus, let's remember, these are not people that played the game via Game Pass, these are people that paid full whack for the game.

Let me be perfectly clear, I am probably the biggest fan of Gears of War to frequent these forums (and I am also a huge Xbox fan) and so I want nothing but success for The Coalition because I want to see many more Gears of War games. I'm just not blind to what is clearly before us, which is that the game is perhaps underperforming. That is the last thing that I want to see, and just because I am highlighting things such as Steam numbers, it does not mean that I am rooting for the game to fail...

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6 is officially a record holder. With a truly funny-sounding 32.5 million copies sold pre-release driving $3.79 billion net sales as of launch day, November 19, Rockstar's latest open-world game is a caliber of commercial, critical, and cultural phenomenon never before seen, even beating out longtime record holders like... other Rockstar games.

Let's unpack that $3.79 billion figure. Sometimes numbers get so big that it can be hard to wrap your head around them. How does GTA 6 compare to other media juggernauts?

As we previously noted, 32.5 million copies sold before even launching sees GTA 6 eclipse Elden Ring's three-year sales of 30 million copies. Those pre-release sales also mean GTA 6 was, per the hastily updated Wikipedia entry for such records, one of the top 30 best-selling games of all time before it even launched.

What about GTA 5, the best-selling game of its kind? Well, way back in 2013, Grand Theft Auto 5 (as Variety noted at the time) earned $800 million in its first day. This was a record for Rockstar at the time.

As I reported in 2018 – holy crap, it's been a while – Red Dead Redemption 2 set the record for the biggest opening weekend with $725 million.

I'm gonna hand the microphone to Past Me for a moment, because I'm pretty sure he's correct: "That record comes with a small caveat: RDR2 released on a Friday and had the best opening weekend ever, not the best opening. The record for the best opening is still held by Rockstar's previous hit, GTA 5, which released on a Tuesday and sold $1 billion in its first three days."

In other words, GTA 6's launch is so big that, one day out of the gate, it has more than doubled the combined openings of GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Here's a more recent comparison. Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey ended its box office run at $1.8 billion globally, making it one of the most profitable films ever. In one day, GTA 6 has more than doubled that.

Avengers: Endgame, meanwhile, ended a very long run around $2.88 billion. Again, after one day, GTA 6 is nearly $1 billion ahead.

Week-end figures from Rockstar will surely be even harder to swallow. There is nobody else in this weight class. By orders of magnitude, we are looking at the biggest entertainment release in history.

#4026. Genshin Impact Luna 7 brings us the first playable Hexenzirkel as things take a turn in Sumeru

Genshin Impact's Luna 7 update will kick off a new Archon Quest chapter, and deliver some interesting new additions to the playable roster.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a new Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major update. Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, or as its friends call it, Luna 7, was unveiled as part of the showcase.

This next update has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

Luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its new Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

If you complete this chapter at launch, you’ll earn up to 560 Primogems, as well as Nicole's Ascension Materials. Nicole is the first of three playable characters arriving with this update. Something else you’ll unlock if you finish the chapter quickly is a new Weekly Boss that HoYo says has “unpredictable abilities.”

And if you haven’t played in a while, don’t worry, you can refer to the Guiding Notes feature to catch you up on what’s been going on in the world. This is part of a larger effort from the team to make story progression more seamless, and also includes improved quest autosave prompts.

Nicole Reeyn is highest-profile and most interesting, being the first playable member of the Hexenzirkel. The mage is a 5-Star Pyro Catalyst wielder intended as a support member of the team. She can boost the ATK of all party members, even those not currently on the field. She also generates a shield while doing so.

Her Elemental Burst allows her to summon an Arcane Projection that follows the active character, sending out Coordinated Attacks that match their Elemental Type. Outside of combat, Nicole can help you find treasures by calling upon a Seelie to guide you to them. Quite fitting, as you’ll be exploring in the inside of the Witch's Lodge in Nicole’s Meeting Point in Luna 7, so bring her along.

Lohen, the Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius' Fifth Company, is the second new character. Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

Prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

Nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a new limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

You’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a new sports festival for you to take part in.

One new gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

Before you pick the game back up, be sure to check out our recently-updated Genshin Impact codes page for some free stuff you may be missing.

#4025. Anniversary: Super Smash Bros. Melee Has Now Been Duking It Out For 25 Years

One first-party title from the GameCube library that's well and truly outlived this particular Nintendo generation is Super Smash Bros. Melee, and today happens to be the game's 25th anniversary in Japan.

After introducing fans to the series in 1999 on the N64, Masahiro Sakurai and the team at HAL Laboratory & Nintendo rolled out this new, improved, and faster take on the all-star Nintendo fighter in November 2001. Not only was it a popular couch game, but Melee went on to have an incredibly successful run as a competitive game.

According to Nintendo's official data, Melee is officially the "best-selling game of all time" for the GameCube, shifting over seven million copies worldwide, with the system itself selling 21.74 million units during its lifetime.

This particular entry was so influential within the Smash scene that it led to Nintendo re-releasing the GameCube controller and making newer entries in the series compatible with this same pad, as it was the preferred pick for any serious or pro player.

To this day, the game's competitive scene is still going strong, with game's meta continuing to evolve, and players like "Hungrybox" (the famous Jigglypuff main) are still knocking about. Of course, there have also been plenty of scandals within the competitive space over the years, but Melee continues to thrive, and is still capable of packing out events across the globe.

So, on behalf of the team here at Nintendo Life, here's to another 25 years of duking it out. Oh, and if Nintendo hasn't already got something planned, now would be the perfect time to add Melee to the Switch 2's GameCube library. For North America, the game's 25th anniversary takes place in early December.

#4024. GTA 6 Doesn't Have Any Sex Workers, and Rockstar Has Explained Why

A mainstay of the GTA series has been the presence of sex workers, but Rockstar Games has dropped this aspect for the newly released GTA 6.

As reported by Shack News, unlike most other games in the long-running franchise, you cannot hire a sex worker in GTA 6.

The outlet asked Rockstar about this decision, and received the following response:

"GTAVI is a game about a couple in a bind, lovers on the run. While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in VI has been done to support the spirit of the story we wanted to tell, and the gameplay systems we wanted to expand upon - things like wanted system, the radio, robberies and car theft. Many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTAVI, but the elements we have we believe are all necessary and complementary to the feeling and motivations we wanted to emphasize as you play through Jason and Lucia's story."

So, in other words, sex workers aren't included this time around because it wouldn't make sense for Jason or Lucia to pursue that, as they're already in a relationship — and that's a big part of the story.

As mentioned, they have been present in the series since 2001's GTA 3, and this will be the first 3D game to exclude them.

GTA 6 is also the first game that centres on a couple, however, with the relationship between Jason and Lucia interwoven in the gameplay as well as being a key tenet of the narrative. It seems Rockstar didn't think sex workers would be conducive to this goal.

#4023. GTA 6 First-Person Glitch Discovered, And It Works On Xbox & PS5

As you probably know, GTA 6 is not a game that's designed to let you freely play in first-person (at least not at launch), but thanks to some sleuthing from various GTA fans, it's been discovered that you can actually play this way.

This is thanks to a glitch that occurs when you change a specific setting and then spam the "View" button (formerly known as the "Back" button) on Xbox to trick the game into forcing you into first-person mode.

Here's how you do it (at your own risk - this is not an intended feature!):

The same instructions apply if you're on PS5, but it's the touchpad rather than the View button.

I've only been messing with this glitch a little bit so far, but it's pretty insane at first glance. You can run around, drive vehicles... do whatever you want to do. The only problem is that you can't actually back out of first-person once you're in it, although it seems some situations (like being arrested or going into a hair salon) will force you back into third-person.

So, why is Rockstar hiding this feature from us? It's probably because it's still in a work-in-progress, and there are some items that don't seem to function properly with the first-person viewpoint yet. This does seem to indicate a first-person perspective is in the works though, similar to how it was added into GTA 5 later down the line.

I'll leave you with some very, very quick screengrabs of my own down below, along with a helpful video that's getting a ton of traction on YouTube explaining how to make it work.

Hutcherson was one of the top choices for Sony's 2012 Spider-Man reboot

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Josh Hutcherson said he gave up on superhero movies after losing the role of Spider-Man in Sony's 2012 reboot of the formerly Sam Raimi-led franchise.

"Since I didn't get cast in Spider-Man, I was like, 'I don't ever want to be a superhero. Like, it's fine. I never really wanted that,'" Hutcherson said on the Happy Sad Confused podcast. "And then Mister Miracle came around, and I read, all I had was like a few of the scenes to do the audition, and it was such a cool character."

Hutcherson was up for the role of Peter Parker/Spider-Man alongside Jamie Bell, Logan Lerman, and Alden Ehrenreich. Luckily for Hutcherson, the loss of Spidey led him to get the role of Peeta Mellark in Francis Lawrence's blockbuster movie franchise based on the dystopian YA book series, Hunger Games.

The animated Mister Miracle series was announced just a couple of months ago with Hutcherson as the lead, with the show being canon to the new DCU... meaning Hutcherson could then go on to reprise the role in a live-action project later on. Sadly, the fate of Mister Miracle is currently up in the air as we don't know what projects will be axed now that James Gunn and Peter Safran are no longer the co-CEOs of DC Studios. So far, it looks like Lanterns season 2 is up on the chopping block.

Next up for Marvel is Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters worldwide on December 18. For more, check out how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

#4021. Mystic Messenger's most loyal players are getting banned in droves for seemingly playing the game too much

With the 10th anniversary of Mystic Messenger nearly upon us, the dating sim has inexplicably begun issuing wide-spread bans for its most active players.

Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving new content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

The message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

It didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

The running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a new automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

The timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large update for Mystic Messenger, which may include new content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

This is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very quickly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

It’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without new content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

#4019. Forza Horizon 6 explodes on Steam even before it's officially out

Forza Horizon 6 looks to have easily delivered the most successful launch for any game in the series on PC, with record-breaking player numbers.

Steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated launches, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

That version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, currently occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

At the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

All of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

Steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

Game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

Forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

#4017. GTA 6 Players Warned To Turn Off Auto-Uploads Or Risk Getting Banned On Xbox

Xbox is handing out bans to GTA 6 players for uploading game captures that 'accidentally' breach its family and online safety guidelines.

On by default, game captures automatically uploaded to Xbox Live servers are scanned for offensive imagery, including hate speech, drugs misuse, excessive violence, as well as nudity and sexual content.

According to some Reddit sleuthing, GTA 6 players are being banned for uploading content captured on the beach in Leonida amongst other activities. The original poster claimed to have captured "zero nudity-just standard Vice City beach/coastal gameplay with NPCs in swimsuits/bikinis" before getting slapped with a ToS violation.

If you think about it, it would be odd to walk around a beach with a video camera filming the locals, but it's a bit silly to see Xbox players getting 2-day bans. The rulings appear to be automated and unappealable too.

It's not clear if sexual content or nudity is the cause for the violation, but it's worth noting GTA 6 does contain full-frontal nudity. We'd recommend not spamming the capture button during those sequences. Xbox doesn't like that sort of thirsty behaviour.

If you're worried about getting a 2-day ban in the height of GTA 6 fever, then perhaps you could consider turning off automatic uploads in your Xbox settings. Here's a quick guide on how to do this:
